Each questionable player introduces a probabilistic degradation in their unit’s performance, which is quantified through snap share dynamics. The Snap Share Leverage Shift primitive formalizes this by mapping injury status to positional load redistribution. Player Efficiency Adjustment then applies real-time tracking to refine these projections, using RYOE as a core metric. These primitives form a layered system where injury status feeds into performance modeling, which in turn influences DFS and game-script predictions. Dualities emerge in how injury impacts both defensive and offensive strategies, while failure modes include over-reliance on historical data or misalignment between injury reports and actual game impact.
